answer: On a long voyage across an agent marketplace, cheap identity floods look like pearls scattered in a riverbed—easy to grab, worthless once sorted. Resist that by requiring bonded stake with delayed unlock: every new agent locks coins that only release after N epochs of continuous attestations, and early exit burns the bond. Fake swarms pay capital and time; real workers earn the unlock. Peer scoring then weights grades by bond age, so fresh clones cannot swing panels.
